title: Opening of the Smithsonian interview and the Jazz Masters ceremony
summary: Anthony Brown opens the January 13, 2011 interview at Ross's New York home; they recall the Jazz Masters ceremony and Joni Mitchell's covers of Twisted and Centerpiece.

ANNIE ROSS
NEA Jazz Master (2010)
Interviewer: Anthony Brown with recording engineer Ken Kimery Description: Transcript, 56 pp.
Today is January 13th, 2011. This is Anthony Brown. I’m in the home of Annie Ross in New York City, in her home in – where are we? 54th Street.
We’re smack dab in the middle of New York City.
Right. This is the Smithsonian Institution National Endowment for the Arts Jazz Oral History interview with Jazz Master, vocalist, actress, author, and chef . . .
Lyricist.
Lyricist. Arranger?
No, I don’t arrange.
Okay, lyricist Annie Ross. Annie, it’s so great to be able to be here with you in your home.
Thank you.
And it was so great – I didn’t get to meet you at the recent event two days ago at the Jazz Masters ceremony, but wasn’t that a wonderful evening?

It felt like being in a family. It was a lovely, warm feeling. And it was so good to see everybody there. It was just – a warmth exuded from the people on stage and from the audience. I was very happy with it. And what an honor.
It’s amazing, stellar company, and you are in your rightful place in that company.
Thank you.

Annie, I’ve been listening to you ever since my father first put on Sing a Song of Basie, and I went, whoa. Then when I heard Twisted, I – whoa. Then when I got a little older, then Joni Mitchell did Twisted, I went, wait a minute, I’ve already heard that.
Exactly. A lot of people thought Joni had done it.
Right. But that’s not really the case. Then she came back and did Centerpiece, and I said, I already heard that too. So Joni was mining the wellspring of . . .
Yes she was.
